Batch 4E skill 4/6 — RETIRES THE LAST UNSIGNED-PREREQ INVERSION (solve_particle_equil_3d). Every signed node's prerequisites are now signed, for the first time since the 98-node graph was committed. SCOPE WAS OPERATOR-DERIVED, not Architect-ruled: the Batch 4E ruling detailed skill 1/6's scope only. Derived from graph truth and the signed boundaries. The Architect's binding 3D ruling was honored — particle-equilibrium debt retirement, not 3D rigid-body expansion: no rigid_body_fbd_3d, no 3D rigid-body equilibrium, and no moment equation, since a particle's forces are concurrent and no moment arises. Three boundaries cleared at the review beat. Against particle_fbd_2d (parent): the 3D case is genuinely new because direction cannot be fixed by one in-plane angle and forces need not share a plane. Against cartesian_vector_components_3d (parent, signed one lane earlier): this skill REPRESENTS each force's given 3D line of action and does NOT resolve it into components — a resolution step would duplicate the parent. Against solve_particle_equil_3d (downstream, signed before its prerequisites existed): that skill's worked example HANDS the student unit vectors and writes SumF = 0 in one line; it consumes a 3D FBD without teaching the inventory. This skill supplies it. Worked example: ring at A with FOUR concurrent forces — W = 100 N along -z from a hanging load, applied P = 60 N along -y, cable AB into the +x/+y/+z octant (phi_AB = 36.9 degrees from +z, theta_AB = 53.1 degrees from +x), cable AC into the -x/+y/+z octant (phi_AC = 36.9 degrees, theta_AC = 126.9 degrees from +x). Deliverable is the labeled inventory with known/unknown classification; magnitudes are not solved. Operator independently verified that this configuration ADMITS equilibrium — u_AB = (0.36, 0.48, 0.80), u_AC = (-0.36, 0.48, 0.80); SumFx gives T_AB = T_AC, SumFy gives 0.96T = 60, SumFz gives 1.60T = 100, both yielding T = 62.5 N consistently — which matters because this FBD must be a valid input to solve_particle_equil_3d. Non-coplanarity verified from the correct criterion: W and P both lie in the yz-plane, so any plane containing both IS the yz-plane, and cable AB has a nonzero +x sense, so no single plane contains all four force lines. 2-signal mapping, content-earned: sign_or_placement_error at step 5 (drawing each force on its 3D line with the right sense), unclassified at step 7 (inventory completeness and scope boundary). axis_confusion correctly OMITTED — no authored step resolves components, consistent with every signed FBD/inventory skill (particle_fbd_2d, rigid_body_fbd_2d, contact_force_modeling); adding it would require a resolution step and duplicate the parent. simple_average_used omitted: Centroids-family signal. PREREQ_N is 2, the multi-parent case, and Architect Batch 4E Decision B governs: canonical four only, mapped to authored steps. Review-beat correction, and the root cause was the OPERATOR CONTRACT rather than the authoring: the original example had THREE forces with both cables pulling +y and nothing opposing them, so no equilibrium existed (SumFy forced both tensions to zero while SumFz demanded their sum be 125). The contract had required at least three forces AND a non-planar layout — jointly unsatisfiable, because three concurrent forces in equilibrium are necessarily coplanar: if F1 + F2 + F3 = 0 then F3 = -(F1 + F2), which lies in the plane of F1 and F2. Genuine 3D particle statics needs four or more forces; the contract never said four, and the draft resolved the conflict by sacrificing the requirement that was left implicit. A fourth force P was added. Three smaller corrections: theta_AC was 53.1 degrees, but a ray into -x/+y makes 126.9 degrees with +x (the parent's 53.1 degrees into +x/-y was legitimate because that unsigned angle from +x really is 53.1 degrees; the -x case is not symmetric that way); the non-coplanarity argument reasoned from COORDINATE planes, which does not establish non-coplanarity — not lying in any plane is what the term means; and formula.variables carried a single 'x, y, z' entry naming three symbols (the same defect corrected on support_reaction_modeling's 'Ax, Ay' entry) while declaring phi and theta generically though the file uses phi_AB, phi_AC, theta_AB, theta_AC. The axes entry was removed, following the just-signed cartesian_vector_components_3d, which declares i/j/k but not the axes. OPERATOR OBSERVATION FOR ARCHITECT, recorded as content debt and not actionable in this lane: the signed solve_particle_equil_3d's own worked example is coplanar in the xz-plane, with y = 0 on both cables. That is not sloppiness — with only three forces it could not have been otherwise, by the coplanarity theorem above. A signed 3D equilibrium skill whose example is necessarily planar is worth an Architect look when the legacy audit reaches it.

Improper constraint detection — a body may pass the count-based determinacy test yet be unable to hold equilibrium because its reactions are arranged all parallel or all concurrent, so a correct reaction count is necessary but not sufficient for proper constraint. THE EQUAL-COUNT CONSTRUCTION IS THE SPINE AND IT HOLDS: all three worked bodies carry n_r = n_e = 3 and pass the count test identically, so arrangement alone separates the verdicts and the skill does not collapse into the determinacy test it extends. Body A, a beam on three vertical rollers, is improper by PARALLEL reactions — with no horizontal reaction component, sum Fx = 0 becomes 0 = the horizontal load and cannot be satisfied, so the beam slides. Body B, a plate held by three links whose lines of action all pass through a common point O, is improper by CONCURRENT reactions — producing no moment about O, sum M about O = 0 becomes 0 = the applied moment about O and cannot be satisfied, so the plate rotates. Each improper mode is made concrete as an equilibrium equation that cannot be satisfied rather than asserted. Body C, a pin plus roller at the SAME count of three, is proper: the pin supplies two independent directions and the roller keeps the lines non-concurrent, so a horizontal load and a moment both find resistance. The arrangement test verifies all three verdicts WITHOUT counting, by two questions — are components present in two independent directions, and do the reaction lines fail to share a common point — with proper constraint requiring both yes: Body A fails the first, Body B the second, Body C passes both. BOUNDARY: constraints_static_determinacy, the signed prerequisite and subtopic sibling, owns the count test, which is cited and taken as given and not re-authored, the complement stated in one sentence that it counts reactions against equations while this skill examines the arrangement of a body that already passes that count. The reaction inventory is taken from the FBD skills, and this artifact explicitly completes the deferral recorded in rigid_body_fbd_3d that six unknowns do not imply proper constraint. No reaction values are solved; improper constraint is detected from geometry as inconsistent or indeterminate equilibrium equations for a general load. The common point O is declared distinct from a computed moment point M_O. Honest limitation recorded: the arrangement screen catches the classic all-parallel and all-concurrent modes for a count-adequate planar body and is not a general proof of stability for every loading, with complex 3D mixed cases possibly needing fuller analysis — passing the screen means the classic improper modes are absent, not that every instability is excluded. One earned signal, unclassified at step 1, the boundary and method fallback for concluding proper constraint from count alone, re-authoring the count test, solving for reactions, or skipping the arrangement exam. axis_confusion was scrutinized specifically, since the parallel and concurrent modes concern directions and lines of action, and correctly omitted: the failure this skill guards against is not examining arrangement at all, a method error caught at step 1, rather than misreading which axis is involved, so mapping axis_confusion onto a geometric-reasoning skill would be padding. sign_or_placement_error, simple_average_used and solution_sequencing_error cannot be earned: no signed quantity or force placement authored, no averaging, and no stranded prerequisite chain. This draft required no correction, the fourth consecutive clean draft, and its artifact was re-delivered in full for the review beat after the lane-closure notice arrived without it.

Batch 4E skill 6/6 — CLOSES BATCH 4E at 39 of 98. SCOPE WAS OPERATOR-DERIVED, not Architect-ruled: the Batch 4E ruling detailed skill 1/6's scope only. STRUCTURAL REASON: the signed support_reaction_modeling (a3e5cba6) catalogs a cable or two-force link as 'one force along the member axis' — a bare assertion. It never states when a body qualifies as a two-force member, and never justifies why the force lies along that line. This skill supplies both: the qualification test and the equilibrium argument. Boundary against support_reaction_modeling verified at the review beat: that skill asserts the reaction shape; this one tests qualification and proves collinearity, and it teaches the chord-versus-shape distinction that skill never mentions. Boundary against rigid_body_equilibrium_2d (the prerequisite): that skill writes and solves the three equations for magnitudes; this one uses the equilibrium argument QUALITATIVELY to establish a structural property and computes nothing. THE ARGUMENT, authored qualitatively as procedure step 4: moments about one application point vanish for the force at the other point only if that force's line of action passes through the first point, so both forces lie on the chord; force equilibrium then makes them equal and opposite. No moment value is computed. THE MISCONCEPTION THIS SKILL OWNS, and the reason the example is built as it is: students believe two pins means two-force, and that the forces run along the member. Both are false. The worked example punishes both. Member AB is an L-shaped BENT link, pinned at A (0,0) and B (4.0, 3.0), with the bar running A to (4.0, 0) to B: the chord direction is the diagonal, verified by Operator as (0.8, 0.6), while the L-legs run (1,0) and (0,1) — so 'along the member' and 'along the chord' are visibly different directions, and a student who follows the member's shape is wrong. Member BC is pinned at B and C with a downward load P at midspan: it FAILS qualification on a real disqualifier, an intermediate applied load between the pins, so a student who treats every two-pin body as two-force misclassifies it. A single qualifying member would have made the test unmeasurable — the same defect family as the single rough interface caught on contact_force_modeling and the symmetric load caught on general_distributed_load_resultant. Hard stops verified absent from every step: no force magnitude computed, no moment value computed, no three-force concurrency (that is the downstream sibling three_force_member_identification, which this sign-off unlocks), no frame or machine disassembly, no truss method, no re-authoring of the support catalog, no 3D. 2-signal mapping, content-earned: sign_or_placement_error at step 3, where the chord is drawn — directing a bent member's forces along its shape instead of along the chord is a placement error, and it is this skill's OWN content, not support_reaction_modeling's, whose sign_or_placement_error sits at its own step 3 on a different decision (the support_reactions_2d catch was checked and does not apply). unclassified at step 6, the report-and-stop step, covering misclassification, omitted disqualifiers, and scope exits. axis_confusion correctly OMITTED: no authored step resolves a force into components, consistent with every signed identification and FBD skill — contact_force_modeling, particle_fbd_3d, rigid_body_fbd_2d, constraints_static_determinacy. simple_average_used omitted: Centroids-family signal. F was removed rather than inserted into the text, because this skill deliberately never names a magnitude. Separately, a solution step carried the sentence 'A student who treats every two-pin body as two-force would wrongly classify BC' — a statement about the diagnostic inside a worked solution.
